extracted.intended_audience: educated readers, naturalists, and students of physical geography, geology, astronomy, and philosophy of science
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing and evaluating the physical description and physical history of the world (cosmography): how to balance empirical observation, historical reconstruction, mathematical treatment, and chemical/qualitative considerations when describing terrestrial and sidereal phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish physical history from physical description
rubrics_metrics.description: We would first distinguish between the physical 'history' and the physical 'description' of the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical history ought to trace variations experienced by the universe through ages (new stars appearing/disappearing, nebulae evolving, formation of early vegetation, uplifted coral reefs). Physical description presents a picture of all that exists in space — the simultaneous action of natural forces and the phenomena they produce. Use history to explain formation; use description to present current state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include historical formation to comprehend present phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: But if we would correctly comprehend nature, we must not entirely or absolutely separate the consideration of the present state of things from that of the successive phases through which they have passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To understand present features (e.g., geological strata, faunas/floras), investigations must look back at modes of formation. Anti-pattern: treating present phenomena as isolated without tracing their genesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geological interpretation requires pursuit of the past
rubrics_metrics.description: The geologist... can not form a conception of the present without pursuing, through countless ages, the history of the past.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret sedimentary strata, fossil succession, and landscape morphology as records of former conditions. Use strata to reconstruct successive faunas and floras; their form is their history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat the sidereal (astronomical) portion as primary, not subordinate
rubrics_metrics.description: In order adequately to estimate the dignity of the Cosmos, it is requisite that the sidereal portion ... should not be made subordinate to the terrestrial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When composing a cosmography, begin with a geographical sketch of the universe (a 'map of the world') and the description of heavenly bodies rather than subordinating them to terrestrial concerns. This preserves proper scale and perspective of cosmic description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer mathematical methods for sidereal science; accept complexity in terrestrial sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: The sidereal portion of the science of the Cosmos is based on the pure and abundant source of mathematical astronomy, as is the terrestrial portion on physics, chemistry, and organic morphology; but the domain of these last-named sciences embraces phenomena so complicated ... that the physical science of the earth can not boast of the same certainty and simplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rigorous mathematical treatment where possible (astronomy); recognize that earth sciences demand integration of physics, chemistry, morphology and may resist the same certainty. Anti-pattern: forcing purely mathematical reduction where specific material properties dominate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize introduction of new terms; expand nomenclature only when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The introduction of new terms, especially with reference to the general results of a science which ought to be accessible to all, has always been greatly in opposition to my own practice; and whenever I have enlarged upon the established nomenclature, it has only been in the specialities of descriptive botany and zoology...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use established terminology for general exposition; coin new names only when new objects require them. Guidance applies especially to works intended for a broad audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine empirical observation with rational thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Science is the labor of mind applied to nature... Science does not present itself to man until mind conquers matter in striving to subject the result of experimental investigation to rational combinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not separate empirical data from intellectual synthesis. Good scientific accounts integrate careful observation/experiment with analysis, hypotheses, and rational generalization. Anti-patterns: pure speculation unanchored in observation; empiricism claiming more than data justify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use hypotheses to guide experiments (rational experimentalism)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rational experimentalist does not proceed at hazard, but acts under the guidance of hypotheses, founded on a half indistinct and more or less just intuition of the connection existing among natural objects or forces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design experiments to test hypotheses derived from observation and intuition. Avoid unguided trial-and-error; experiments should aim to evoke phenomena under determined conditions to produce empirical laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify and group phenomena to discover general laws
rubrics_metrics.description: It is only by distributing them into groups that we have been able ... to discover the empire of certain natural laws, grand and simple as nature itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize observations into classes, orders, families and seek analogies and differences to generalize laws. Apply strict reasoning to analogous phenomena to extend laws' scope. Anti-pattern: treating facts as disconnected without seeking patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize two forms of abstraction: quantity (mathematics) and quality (chemistry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two forms of abstraction conjointly regulate our knowledge, namely, relations of 'quantity', comprising ideas of number and size, and relations of 'quality', embracing the consideration of the specific properties and the heterogeneous nature of matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the appropriate intellectual approach: mathematical abstraction for quantitative relations, chemical/qualitative analysis for material properties. Do not attempt to reduce qualitative chemical phenomena solely to mechanical/mathematical laws when specific properties intervene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge limits and incompleteness of experimental sciences
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental sciences, based on the observation of the external world, can not aspire to completeness; the nature of things, and the imperfection of our organs, are alike opposed to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report findings with humility about limits of observation and instrumentality; expect that no generation will exhaust nature's phenomena. Avoid overclaiming universality from limited data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid forcing a single unifying principle across incompatible domains
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle of unity is lost sight of, and the guiding clew is rent asunder whenever any specific and peculiar kind of action manifests itself amid the active forces of nature... the law of equivalents and the numerical proportions of composition ... still remains isolated and independent of mathematical laws of motion and gravitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept that different domains (e.g., chemical composition vs mechanical laws) may have their own governing principles. Valuable synthesis seeks connections but respects domain-specific independence. Anti-pattern: insisting on a single explanatory framework when evidence shows distinct laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical description should show simultaneous action of natural forces
rubrics_metrics.description: The physical description of the world presents a picture of all that exists in space -- of the simultaneous action of natural forces, together with the phenomena which they produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing environments, present interactions of forces (climate, geology, biology) as co-occurring processes, not just isolated phenomena. Use this approach to give a holistic account of present conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate comparative geography and human history where relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: The delineation of comparative geography, drawn in its full extent, and in all its relations with the history of man, ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In geographic/cosmographic works, relate physical descriptions to human history and distribution of peoples when appropriate. Comparative geography should connect natural features with human activity and historical processes.
